name: Tranquility Base
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Statio Tranquillitatis (0.6741°N, 23.4732°E)
notes: Flat, equatorial mare basalt plain, the first crewed landing site. Smooth, dark lava terrain with a full day-night thermal cycle.

name: Von Kármán crater (Chang'e-4)
mission: Chang'e-4 landing site (Statio Tianhe) · lunar far side, South Pole–Aitken basin
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Statio Tianhe, Chang'e-4 landing site (45.45°S, 177.6°E)
notes: Mare-flooded floor of a large crater inside the South Pole–Aitken basin, the first landing on the lunar far side.

name: Statio Shiv Shakti (Chandrayaan-3)
mission: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram landing site · lunar south polar highlands
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Statio Shiv Shakti, Chandrayaan-3 Vikram landing site (69.3734°S, 32.3198°E)
notes: High-latitude highland plain near the south pole, with low sun angles and long shadows but outside the permanently shadowed zone.

name: Shackleton crater rim
mission: Artemis III candidate region · lunar south pole
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Shackleton crater centre (89.67°S, 129.78°E; diameter 20.9 km); the 50 km window centred here contains the whole rim and lies well inside LOLA LDEM_75S_240M coverage
notes: Rim of a 21 km crater almost at the south pole: near-permanent sunlight on the rim beside a permanently shadowed, very cold interior.

name: Jezero crater (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
mission: Mars 2020 Perseverance landing site · Jezero crater, western Isidis
coord_source: Newman et al. 2022, Sci. Adv. 8, eabn3783: “Perseverance landed at longitude 77.45°E and latitude 18.44°N”
notes: Floor of a 45 km crater that once held a lake, next to a river delta. Ancient lake sediments and igneous crater-floor rocks.

name: Gale crater (Bradbury Landing)
mission: Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity landing site · Aeolis Palus, Gale crater
coord_source: Vasavada et al. 2014, JGR Planets 119, “Overview of the Mars Science Laboratory mission: Bradbury Landing to Yellowknife Bay and beyond” (4.5895°S, 137.4417°E)
notes: Crater-floor plain below the 5 km layered mound of Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp), with ancient lake mudstones and active dunes.

name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
mission: Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity landing site · Eagle crater, Meridiani Planum
coord_source: Squyres et al. 2004 (Opportunity Athena science overview, Science): lander at 1.9462°S, 354.4734°E (IAU 2000, MOLA-tied triangulation)
notes: Very flat equatorial plain of sulfate-rich sandstones covered with hematite spherules, recording past acidic groundwater.

name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
mission: InSight lander site · western Elysium Planitia
coord_source: Golombek et al. 2020, Nat. Commun. 11, 1014 (4.502°N, 135.623°E); refined to 4.502384°N, 135.623447°E in Golombek et al. 2020, Earth Space Sci.
notes: One of the smoothest, flattest equatorial lava plains on Mars, chosen for safety; thin regolith over Hesperian–Amazonian basalt.

name: Phoenix landing site
mission: Phoenix lander site · Vastitas Borealis, near Heimdal crater
coord_source: Smith et al. 2009, Science 325, 58 (“H2O at the Phoenix Landing Site”): 68.22°N, 234.25°E areocentric
notes: Arctic plain of ice-cemented polygonal ground; water ice lies a few centimetres below the soil.

name: Utopia Planitia (Zhurong)
mission: Tianwen-1 Zhurong rover landing site · southern Utopia Planitia
coord_source: Liu et al. 2023, Natl. Sci. Rev. 10, nwad056 (109.925°E, 25.066°N; elevation −4099.4 m)
notes: Low northern plain near the dichotomy boundary, with troughs, cones and wind ripples, thought to hold buried ice-related deposits.

name: Arcadia Planitia
mission: Candidate region for human landing with shallow ground ice · northern lowlands
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Arcadia Planitia feature centre (49.02°N, 188.15°E); a regional centre, not a specific landing point
notes: Smooth mid-latitude lowland plain where orbital radar and fresh craters point to water ice within metres of the surface.

name: Deuteronilus Mensae
mission: Mesas with debris-covered glaciers · dichotomy boundary, northern mid-latitudes
coord_source: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Deuteronilus Mensae feature centre (45.1095°N, 23.9184°E); a regional centre, not a specific landing point
notes: Flat-topped mesas and valleys along the dichotomy boundary, surrounded by lobate debris aprons made of buried glacial ice.
